title: A Man Who Keeps Moving
summary: Open on Kael as an ordinary drifter crossing the Sunfields in Jessa's battered rig. The narrator establishes the simple truth of who he is before anyone else gets a chance to rename him.

panelPlan.text: Wide opening panel across the top: hard white Sunfields under a huge pale sky. Jessa's battered rig is a small moving shape on the road, with a half-buried black Sunforge rib far off the shoulder being used by two travelers as shade.
Inside the rig, Kael rides with one boot braced against the floor, hat low, watching the road rather than Jessa. His satchel is at his feet.
Jessa drives one-handed, goggles pushed up, glancing at a heat shimmer ahead where low buildings begin to resolve.
Small final panel: a hand-painted board appears through the glare: LAST DROP — WATER / SHADE / ROOMS.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not because anybody ran him out of anywhere. He just tends to keep moving.

directionInline.text: Establish the narrator immediately as dry, factual and slightly amused. It may know ordinary facts about people but does not know or explain the larger mystery. Do not make the opening ominous.

title: One Drink
summary: Jessa drops Kael at the Last Drop for water and food. Their existing arrangement is casual enough that neither calls it companionship yet, but Jessa expects him back at the rig.

panelPlan.text: The rig rolls into the Last Drop settlement: patched roofs, hitching rails, shaded tables, people doing ordinary midday work. The saloon is the darkest doorway in town.
Jessa brakes beside a water trough. Kael lifts his satchel, then leaves it on the floor after a glance at the saloon.
Kael steps down into the glare. Jessa leans across the empty seat and nudges his satchel farther from the door with two fingers.
Kael notices what she did. Jessa has already turned forward again.
He heads toward the saloon while Jessa steers the rig toward shade behind a low outbuilding.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: JESSA PETRESCU gave him a ride yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither of them has discussed whether that arrangement is still in effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'll try not to offend it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Because then you'll come back for it.

directionInline.text: Their chemistry should already have mild friction and familiarity, but not intimacy. Jessa is practical, not possessive; Kael is amused enough not to argue about the bag.

title: Nothing Ever Happens Here
summary: Meet Eva as a bored sixteen-year-old embedded in the Last Drop's ordinary social life. She notices the scarred patron notice Kael before she has any reason to care about him herself.

panelPlan.text: Inside the Last Drop before Kael enters: dim room, patched bar, flies at the window, lunch plates, card game, boots on chairs. Eva wipes the same stretch of bar for the third time while the bartender counts coins nearby.
Eva watches a traveler outside through the doorway, then looks back at the card game with disappointment.
At a side table, the scarred patron has a folded scrap beside his cup. He glances from the scrap toward the bright doorway.
Kael's silhouette crosses the threshold. The patron goes completely still.
Eva catches the change in him before she fully looks at Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: She has spent most of the summer waiting for something to happen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: If I wipe this spot again, I think it becomes a religious practice.

directionInline.text: Eva belongs to the place before she leaves it. Give the Last Drop ordinary rhythms and familiar faces. The patron's reaction should be the first break in her boredom.

title: Varnok
summary: The scarred patron calls Kael Varnok before Kael has done anything but enter. The narrator confirms for the reader that Kael genuinely has never heard the name.

panelPlan.text: Large panel: Kael just inside the doorway, still squinting from the glare. The patron stands from his table in the foreground.
Close on the patron. He says the name with recognition and old anger, not uncertainty.
Kael looks over one shoulder toward the door, genuinely checking whether someone else entered behind him.
Eva stops wiping the bar. Several locals glance between the two men.
The patron's hand closes around his bottle. Kael raises one empty hand, more confused than defensive.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Depending on who tells it around the Last Drop, Varnok was a thief, a killer, a hero, or all three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry. You've got the wrong man.

directionInline.text: This is the title-fakeout safeguard. The narrator is authoritative about Kael's ordinary identity, so the audience is not asked to wonder whether he is simply lying. The mystery is why the room is so sure.

title: A Bottle
summary: The patron throws a bottle and then himself. Kael reacts efficiently without turning the room into a showdown; Eva's curiosity becomes personal because Kael refuses to behave like the returning outlaw everyone expects.

panelPlan.text: The bottle leaves the patron's hand. Kael tilts aside; glass breaks against the doorframe behind him.
Two nearby patrons shift chairs back. One hand drifts toward a holster, but nobody draws.
The scarred patron lunges. Kael catches his wrist and shoulder instead of striking him.
Kael turns with the momentum and folds the man chest-down across an empty table. Cups jump but do not spill.
Eva has moved closer without realizing it, rag still in one hand.
Kael releases the patron immediately and takes one step back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scarred patron
dialogueInline.text: You think I don't remember you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I think you don't know me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That does seem to be the problem.

directionInline.text: No martial-arts flourish. Kael's physical competence is practical and proportionate. Eva should be intrigued by the mismatch between the room's expectation and Kael's behavior.

title: The Darkest Table
summary: Kael ends the confrontation by sitting down rather than claiming the room. Eva brings him water and invites herself into the empty chair opposite.

panelPlan.text: The patron stays bent over the table catching his breath. Kael rights the chair the man knocked aside.
Kael crosses to the darkest table against the wall. The room remains tense because everyone expected a second act.
Kael sits, removes his gloves and looks toward the bar.
Eva sets a chipped cup of water in front of him. She keeps the second chair pulled out with one foot.
Kael drinks half the cup before looking at her. She sits anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Could I get some water, please?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Good, because I don't have the explanation.

directionInline.text: Let the room remain active around them. Background locals whisper, resume eating, or keep watching. The story does not freeze into a two-shot just because Eva sits down.

title: Problems He Understands
summary: Eva tries to turn the encounter into a mystery. Kael is more interested in water and lunch, and accidentally reveals just enough guardedness to make Eva more curious.

panelPlan.text: Eva leans forward over the table while Kael drinks. A plate of bread, beans and something fried lands between them.
Kael begins eating. Eva waits exactly one bite before continuing.
Kael glances toward the scarred patron across the room, who is now whispering to another local.
Eva catches the glance and mistakes it for concern. Kael notices that she noticed.
His reply about other problems comes out more personal than he intended. He immediately returns his attention to the plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: He knew a face. Mine happened to be standing there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I've got enough problems I already understand, I don't much care about ones I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Bah. Leave it alone. I didn't mean anything by that.

directionInline.text: Protect the approved Kael voice. He is conversational and grammatical, not cryptic. His accidental self-disclosure and retreat should feel like a natural boundary, not a mystery tease.

title: The Story Starts Moving
summary: While Kael eats, the room begins converting the encounter into a Varnok story in real time. Eva hears contradictions accumulate and realizes Kael's indifference is not stopping the narrative from growing around him.

panelPlan.text: Across the room, the scarred patron tells two locals something in a low voice. One reacts with disbelief, the other with excitement.
At another table, a different local looks Kael over and quietly disagrees about some remembered detail.
Eva hears fragments from both conversations while Kael tears bread into his beans.
The bartender sets a refill down and tells Kael the back door is available if he wants it.
Kael looks toward the bright front door, then toward Eva occupying his table like she owns half of it.
At the doorway behind Eva, Jessa appears carrying Kael's satchel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Varnok had gray in his hair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You are remarkably committed to lunch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: It hasn't accused me of anything.

directionInline.text: This page dramatizes social mutation rather than explaining it. Different locals should have different memories and motives. End on Jessa's arrival as the page turn into the travel relationship.

title: Too Hot Here
summary: Jessa has read the town's social temperature from outside and brought Kael's satchel. Her casual 'we' surprises him more than the warning itself; Eva immediately tries to join the arrangement.

panelPlan.text: Jessa stands just inside the saloon doorway with Kael's satchel over one shoulder. She surveys the room before addressing him.
Kael looks at the satchel, then at her. Eva looks between them with new interest.
Jessa nods toward the window, where three locals have begun gathering outside near the rig.
Kael stands, still holding the last piece of bread.
Eva rises too, as though this has already been decided.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: It's too hot here for you. We're leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Fine. I'm leaving. You can come with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I haven't decided whether you're helping.

directionInline.text: Jessa reads people, not prophecy. Her use of 'we' is practical and slightly presumptuous. Eva should clock the relationship instantly and begin inserting herself into it.

title: What Jessa Saw
summary: Outside, Jessa explains the practical reason for leaving: people are beginning to gather around a story rather than an event. Eva interprets Jessa's readiness to leave as evidence that Jessa trusts Kael more than she admits.

panelPlan.text: The three step into the white glare. Jessa walks straight toward the rig while Kael adjusts the satchel she handed back.
Across the street, the small knot of locals glance openly at Kael. One points toward the rear of the saloon.
Eva walks backward in front of Jessa, asking questions while Jessa keeps moving.
Kael pauses to tie the satchel strap. Eva and Jessa get several steps ahead and continue talking about him as if he is not present.
Kael looks up at the sound of his own name but does not interrupt yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had his bag before he agreed to go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: There were three men outside deciding whether they remembered him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I believe what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the first real Eva/Jessa relationship scene. The subject is Kael, but the deeper content is how each woman decides what she believes about a person.

title: Behind the Saloon
summary: The trio is almost out when noise behind the saloon draws Kael around the corner. The issue turns from social inconvenience to immediate human danger.

panelPlan.text: Jessa reaches the rig and starts checking the front wheel while Eva hovers nearby. Kael approaches from behind.
A dull wooden knock comes from the back lot, followed by a choking sound too quiet to be a shout.
Kael stops. Jessa keeps working for one beat, then notices he stopped.
Kael walks toward the rear corner of the saloon. Eva starts after him. Jessa closes her eyes briefly because she knows they are no longer leaving in ten minutes.
Page-turn panel from Kael's viewpoint: only a pair of boots visible beyond the corner, kicking several inches above the dirt.

directionInline.text: Use the page turn. Do not reveal the full hanging until Page 12. Jessa's frustration is affectionate only in hindsight; right now it is practical recognition of Kael's inability to ignore an immediate problem.

title: Dead Weight
summary: Reveal Tomas being publicly hanged in the back lot while Marcus and several locals watch. Kael does not ask for the history before intervening.

panelPlan.text: Large reveal panel: Tomas hangs from a loading beam behind the saloon, boots scraping empty air. Marcus Kovacs stands with two locals nearby as if supervising unpleasant work.
Kael takes in the rope, the beam and the barrel beneath it in one glance.
Marcus turns toward him, irritated at the interruption rather than ashamed.
Kael drags the barrel under Tomas and climbs onto it.
He shoulders Tomas's weight and pulls a knife to the rope.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Behind the Last Drop, Marcus Kovacs is hanging a man named Tomas.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kael does not know Tomas either.

directionInline.text: The narrator supplies only facts. Kael's action should precede any moral speech. He helps because a man is currently choking, not because he has diagnosed the town.

title: Cut the Rope
summary: Kael cuts Tomas down while Marcus invokes Varnok again. Eva arrives in time to see Kael prioritize Tomas over the accusation.

panelPlan.text: Kael saws through the rope while Tomas's weight drives him awkwardly into the barrel.
The rope parts. Kael and Tomas both fall hard into the dirt.
Kael rolls Tomas onto his side and works the noose loose from his neck.
Marcus advances holding a short length of pipe. Eva appears at the corner with the water cup she grabbed from inside.
Tomas coughs violently. Kael looks relieved for exactly one breath.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You always did have to make trouble, Varnok.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't know Varnok. I know this man is choking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Same righteous act. Same damn timing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Easy, Tomas. Don't try to talk yet.

directionInline.text: Kael can learn Tomas's name from somebody shouting it during the rescue or from Tomas himself in a rasp; keep that incidental. The important beat is that Kael's attention remains on the present-tense person.

title: Marcus's Varnok
summary: Marcus tries to force Kael into Varnok's old role by naming grievances and daring him to deny them. Kael keeps refusing the premise and tending Tomas, which frustrates Marcus more than a duel would.

panelPlan.text: Marcus plants himself between Kael and the open yard, pipe loose in one hand. Several locals have gathered at a cautious distance.
Kael kneels beside Tomas, supporting his shoulders while Eva trickles water over Tomas's lips.
Marcus names an old offense. Kael does not look up.
Marcus steps closer, forcing Kael finally to stand between him and Tomas.
Eva sees that the locals are now watching Marcus's behavior rather than simply accepting his version of Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You burned my brother out of this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Look me in the face and say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm looking at him right now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's making this harder.

directionInline.text: Marcus should not sound like he is delivering backstory for the reader. Give him personal anger and need for acknowledgment. Kael's refusal deprives him of the scene he expected.

title: The Wrong Fight
summary: Marcus swings first. Kael avoids him without escalating into a duel, and the conflict becomes visibly less about Varnok than Marcus's need to maintain control in front of the town.

panelPlan.text: Marcus swings the pipe at Kael's head. Kael leans away; the pipe splinters a fence post.
Kael catches Marcus's forearm on the return swing and redirects him into the wall rather than striking him.
Marcus shoves free, humiliated. A local behind him quietly lowers the hand that had been hovering near a holster.
Tomas coughs from the ground. Eva turns back to him rather than watching the fight.
Kael steps away from Marcus and kneels again beside Tomas, exposing his back for a moment because he is choosing the injured man over the contest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I don't have a reason to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Good. Keep him on his side.

directionInline.text: Kael's dry line should not turn the scene into a quip-fest. His real choice is physical: he returns to Tomas while Marcus still wants the audience.

title: Who Is Watching Whom
summary: Marcus discovers that the crowd's attention has shifted. One local helps Tomas without permission, weakening Marcus's control more than Kael could have by defeating him.

panelPlan.text: A woman from the watching crowd steps forward with a folded cloth and kneels beside Tomas.
Another local brings a fresh bucket without being told. Marcus sees both acts.
Kael moves aside enough to let them help. Eva watches the social geometry change.
Marcus raises the pipe again, but nobody moves with him this time.
From beyond the lot comes the rising growl of Jessa's rig.

directionInline.text: This is consequence through community behavior, not a speech. Marcus loses some authority because people act independently while he is focused on the Varnok story.

title: The Rig
summary: Jessa drives into the back lot and turns the possibility of leaving into an immediate choice. Kael makes sure Tomas is in local hands before moving.

panelPlan.text: Jessa's rig slews into the back lot in a low cloud of dust, stopping close enough to make the open passenger door an argument.
Jessa takes in Tomas, Marcus, Kael and Eva in one sweep. Her expression says none of this surprises her enough.
Kael checks Tomas once more with the local woman while Jessa drums two fingers on the wheel.
Marcus moves to block Kael's path to the rig. The locals do not close ranks behind him.
Kael stands and hands the cut length of rope to Marcus instead of a weapon.

directionInline.text: Jessa does not rescue Kael from a fight; she supplies motion. Kael leaves only after another person has taken responsibility for Tomas.

title: Kael Mack
summary: Marcus asks the question the whole issue has been circling. Kael answers with his actual name and leaves Marcus to decide whether to believe it.

panelPlan.text: Marcus blocks the passenger door, pipe lowered but still in hand.
Kael stops rather than forcing past him. Jessa waits behind the wheel, watching Marcus more than Kael.
Marcus looks at Kael with less certainty than before.
Kael gives his name plainly.
Marcus shifts just enough for Kael to pass, not conceding belief.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: You can keep thinking that. It's still my name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then you can tell him about me if he comes back.

directionInline.text: Do not play the last line as a cool-guy mic drop. Kael is tired of the argument and genuinely means Marcus should save it for the person he wants.

title: The Third Passenger
summary: Kael climbs into the rig and discovers Eva has already attached herself to the departure. Jessa refuses to stop long enough for Kael to win the argument.

panelPlan.text: Kael climbs into the passenger seat. Jessa immediately starts rolling before the door is fully shut.
Kael looks in the side mirror and sees Eva on the rear step with a small pack.
He twists in his seat. Eva gives him a small wave.
Jessa keeps her eyes on the road as they clear the settlement.
Kael looks at Jessa. Jessa does not look back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Why is that your answer to everything?

directionInline.text: Eva's departure should feel opportunistic and prepared rather than fated. Jessa's refusal to stop is funny because it is also the practical reason Eva successfully joins them.

title: Before He Walked In
summary: Once the Last Drop is behind them, Eva reveals the scrap she took from the patron's table. The fact that it predates Kael's arrival turns the encounter from a strange resemblance into a real question.

panelPlan.text: Long horizontal: the rig travels across hard white ground. The Last Drop has become a low smudge behind them.
Eva shifts from the rear step into a safer perch and pulls a folded scrap from inside her wrap.
Close on the paper: rough description of a dark-haired man in a dark coat and the words VARNOK COMES THROUGH TODAY.
Kael reads it once. Jessa watches him in the mirror rather than turning around.
Kael hands it back without the reaction Eva wanted.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The paper was on the table before Kael walked in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He had this before you walked in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I rescued it from being evidence nobody noticed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It says Varnok would come through today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then whoever wrote it got the name wrong.

directionInline.text: The note is the issue's actual mystery hook. Keep it mundane paper, ordinary handwriting and plausible human provenance. The oddity is timing, not visual magic.

title: Careful Answers
summary: Eva and Jessa compare what they believe about Kael while he can plainly hear them. Their theories about him begin functioning as the first real conversation between the two women.

panelPlan.text: Eva leans between the seats from behind, still holding the note. Jessa keeps driving.
Eva points out that Jessa had Kael's bag ready before he decided to leave.
Jessa answers without taking the bait completely. Kael stares out the side window, listening.
Eva studies Jessa instead of Kael for the first time.
Kael finally interrupts when the conversation becomes openly about whether Jessa trusts him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: The day is the part I don't like.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't agreeing with you. I was narrowing the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You still had his bag ready before any of this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Marcus had a pipe before any of this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I trust what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can still hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the deliberate early Kael-centered Eva/Jessa dialogue architecture. Their disagreement about what counts as evidence reveals how each woman thinks and creates the first intimacy between them.

title: Dust on the Lens
summary: The accidental trio continues into the Sunfields. Kael remains himself; the Varnok story remains behind them but has already begun moving independently, establishing both the group and the series engine.

panelPlan.text: Wide panel: the rig passes a half-buried black Sunforge shape where two workers have hung a shade cloth from it. Nobody in the rig comments on it.
Inside, Eva folds the note carefully and keeps it. Kael sees her do it and decides not to ask for it back.
Kael looks from Eva to Jessa, then out at the empty road ahead.
Jessa asks the practical question nobody has answered yet.

Final wide panel: the rig small against the Sunfields, three figures now traveling together. In a narrow inset at the bottom, back at the Last Drop, two locals are already retelling the hanging to someone who was not there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Do either of you know where we're going?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By sundown, Kael Mack is still a drifter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Back at the Last Drop, Varnok has already started traveling too.

directionInline.text: End on two simultaneous beginnings: the trio and the independent social life of the false identity. The Sunforge remains ordinary background texture. The narrator may create irony, but should not explain why any of this is happening.
